question: Does the 2023 Pantabangan fisherfolk paper provide site-resolved biological evidence, or only questionnaire and secondary landing context?

source.citation: Tad-o, A. B., Ayanan Jr., D. A., Barangan, T. G., Bautista, J. C., Gagelonia, J. D., Galayugo, A. C., Hoggang, C. G. B., Kiw-is, K. B., Madrid, F. G. N., Ramos, H. A. R., Tacaca, J. O., Tolentino, C. R. S., Ziegler, J. T., & Reyes, A. T. (2023). Assessment of fisherfolk profile and their awareness and belief regarding introduced American largemouth bass Micropterus salmoides in Pantabangan reservoir. AACL Bioflux, 16(4), 2097-2113.
source.access: Publisher-hosted full-text PDF reviewed. No local copy retained.
source.license: The article states that it is distributed under a Creative Commons Attribution License and permits reuse with author and source credit. The article does not state a license version in the reviewed notice.
source.licenseLimit: Do not reuse Figure 1: it is a satellite image credited to Google Maps (2022), and its separate terms were not assessed. No figures, photographs, tables, or extended passages are reproduced in this review.

studyScope.purpose: Socioeconomic profile, respondent experience fishing for introduced American largemouth bass, beliefs about its effects, and stated willingness to take possible interventions.
studyScope.samplingDescription: One face-to-face structured questionnaire survey. The methods call respondents 'randomly chosen using haphazard sampling', an internally inconsistent selection description. Respondents were recruited in communities around the reservoir.
reportedFishingGroundLabels: Barangay Poblacion / West Poblacion (wording varies within the article)
studyScope.biologicalSampling: The described methods are interviews and questionnaires; no fish capture protocol, independently examined specimens, vouchers, or taxon-by-station biological data are reported.
studyScope.spatialLimits: The paper gives broad reservoir bounds including a malformed latitude value, 16°88′ N, and describes multiple municipalities across Nueva Ecija, Nueva Vizcaya, and Aurora. The printed bounds are unusable as geometry. Community fishing-ground names are not capture coordinates or mapped boundaries.
studyScope.figureRights: Figure 1 is a Google Maps satellite image; it was not copied, georeferenced, traced, or used to derive reservoir geometry.

respondentReportedBassContext.reportedCatchRecency: All respondents reportedly identified June 2022 as the latest month and year they caught largemouth bass; this is retrospective questionnaire information, not a dated, independently verified occurrence event.
respondentReportedBassContext.interpretation: These are respondent-reported/estimated fishery context. The paper itself says the effort estimate needs validation and that population trend is indeterminate without accurate catch-per-unit-effort data. Do not publish as catch rates, abundance, present-day status, or location-specific occurrences.

dietBeliefQuestion.question: Respondents were asked whether they thought largemouth bass eats other fishes that might reduce the number of fish caught.
dietBeliefQuestion.interpretation: These percentages describe fisherfolk beliefs, not stomach-content analysis, observed predation, prey taxa, or a species-specific diet finding from this survey. The paper later uses 'cannibalistic' while discussing eating other fishes, but it does not identify prey as conspecifics; this questionnaire cannot establish cannibalism.

secondaryLandingSummary.attribution: The paper attributes the following aggregate landing-center totals to a separate BFAR Region III (2022) NSAP data report. That underlying report and its row-level records were not retrieved in this review.
secondaryLandingSummary.discrepancyDisposition: The nine printed row values sum to 343.85 MT, which is 1.53 MT below the stated 345.38 MT total. The unlisted amount and whether the printed categories are exhaustive are unresolved; do not repair or allocate the difference.
secondaryLandingSummary.spatialAndEvidenceLimits: The summary is secondary, aggregated landing-center context. The paper provides no individual landing events, underlying NSAP records, station-specific taxon matrix, vouchers, or capture coordinates. Landing-center names do not establish where fish were caught.

relationshipsAndLimits.generalDietLiterature: The paper cites external largemouth-bass diet and ecology literature, but this questionnaire did not sample stomach contents. General diet literature must be reviewed and cited separately for any species diet page.
relationshipsAndLimits.reuseAndProjection: The article's stated attribution license does not grant rights to the underlying 2022 BFAR NSAP report, which was not reviewed. Do not redistribute that report's records or convert the secondary aggregate summary into app-ready occurrence rows.

nextAction: If stronger Pantabangan fish evidence is needed, seek a separately licensed primary biological survey or reconcile the cited BFAR Region III NSAP report through a lawful source. Request event-level dates, landing-center definitions, source rows behind the 345.38 MT total, capture-water attribution, taxon identification basis, and reuse terms. Keep respondent reports separate from specimen-based evidence and do not infer present-day presence or absence.
